## Intro

This edition covers the week of 30 November - 6 December 2026 and reports developments for commercial road freight in Germany, Austria, Estonia, Azerbaijan, Belarus and Denmark, with priority for heavy, oversize and special transport. Reports: 14th Lang-Lkw amendment in force: Type 1 extended to 2033, up to 18.41 m with extended cab; Austria: digital vignette only from 1 December 2026; new HGV toll tariff system and CEMT permit digitalisation passed; Estonia to close its road border with Russia on 1 December; Latvia considering similar step.

This edition was prepared after its scheduled release on 2026-11-27T11:00:00.000Z. It covers 2026-W49; the publication date above records the delayed release.

## Lead reports

### 14th Lang-Lkw amendment in force: Type 1 extended to 2033, up to 18.41 m with extended cab (Germany)

The 14th Lang-Lkw-Änderungsverordnung (dated 18 November, published 20 November in BGBl. I Nr. 345) has applied since 21 November 2026. According to the report, Type 1 (tractor plus semi-trailer) is extended until 2033. The existing 17.88 m overall length limit stays. A new exception allows up to 18.41 m, but only for Type 1 with a two-axle tractor where the excess length comes solely from an extended cab per Annex XIII of the implementing regulation. The report also mentions new routes.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Germany – Lang-Lkw network (route details not given in the supplied summary).  
**Affected vehicles:** Lang-Lkw Type 1 (semi-trailer combination) with a two-axle tractor and extended cab for the 18.41 m exception; other combinations are not covered by the new length limit.  
**When:** In force since 21 November 2026; Type 1 authorisation extended to 2033.

**Impact:** Dispatchers must check the exact combination against the rule: the 18.41 m limit does not apply to other Lang-Lkw types or to tractors that do not meet the cab and axle conditions. The extended Type 1 authorisation gives longer planning certainty for fleets using these combinations.

**Recommended action:** Check each Lang-Lkw combination against the BGBl. I Nr. 345 text (cab per Annex XIII, two-axle tractor) and the current positive-route list before dispatch. Update vehicle documentation and routing data.

**Exemptions/conditions:** The 18.41 m exception applies only where the excess length is caused solely by the extended cab. This is an industry blog report on the published regulation; rely on the Federal Law Gazette text for legal conditions.

*Source: [Christians Blog](https://christiansblog.eu/post/bkf/bmvlangehuette/) — Industry report — not an official authority notice*

### Austria: digital vignette only from 1 December 2026; new HGV toll tariff system and CEMT permit digitalisation passed

The Nationalrat passed the amendment to the Bundesstraßen-Mautgesetz. Sticker vignettes (including 1-day, 10-day and 2-month vignettes) are replaced by the digital vignette from 1 December 2026. The package also contains a new tariff system for the LKW-Maut. Parliament separately passed unanimously the CEMT digitalisation law, which covers cross-border goods transport permits.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Austria – federal motorway and expressway network.  
**Affected vehicles:** The vignette change mainly concerns vehicles using the vignette system. The new LKW-Maut tariff system concerns heavy goods vehicles. The exact tariff values and start date of the HGV tariffs are not given in the supplied summary.  
**When:** Digital-only vignette from 1 December 2026.

**Impact:** Heavy-vehicle operators in Austria must expect changed LKW-Maut tariffs under the new system. The CEMT digitalisation changes how cross-border transport permits are handled. The source was published in November 2025 but takes effect in this week.

**Recommended action:** Check the official Austrian HGV toll tariff tables and the CEMT permit procedure before 1 December. Update toll cost calculations for Austria-related quotations and contracts.

**Exemptions/conditions:** No exemptions are stated in the supplied summary. The HGV tariff details and the CEMT digitalisation start date need confirmation from the ASFINAG and ministry publications.

*Source: [Parlament Österreich](https://portal.dapps.prod.k8.parlament.gv.at/aktuelles/pk/jahr_2025/pk1046)*

### Estonia to close its road border with Russia on 1 December; Latvia considering similar step

According to a Times of Central Asia analysis republished by Eurasian Annals, Estonia will close its road border with Russia on 1 December, citing national security. Latvia is reportedly considering a similar move. The report says Central Asian carriers face fewer routes to Europe and potentially higher costs, while Caspian Sea alternatives are limited by capacity, cost and unpredictable delivery times.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Estonia–Russia road border crossings; possible Latvian measures under consideration (not decided). Specific crossings and the handling of goods traffic are not detailed in the supplied summary.  
**Affected vehicles:** Road freight vehicles on routes between Russia/Central Asia and the EU; the exact scope of the closure for goods vehicles is not confirmed in the supplied text.  
**When:** Closure announced for 1 December 2026.

**Impact:** Carriers using Estonian crossings for traffic to or from Russia and Central Asia need alternative routings, with longer transit times and higher costs. This is an industry report, not an official notice.

**Recommended action:** Verify the closure scope with Estonian border authorities and customers, and re-plan affected loads before 1 December. Do not assume Latvian crossings will stay open.

**Exemptions/conditions:** None stated in the source.

*Source: [Eurasian Annals (citing The Times of Central Asia)](https://eurasianannals.gr/index.php/business-news/analyseis/central-asian-trade-routes-to-europe-face-growing-restrictions) — Industry report — regulatory/route conditions require confirmation with the competent authority*

## Rest of Europe: sourced operational reports

### Azerbaijan: complaints over oversize and over-height transport; special permit and fee rules cited

A Turkish exporters' chamber circular (DENİB, 19 November 2026), citing the Turkish Trade Ministry and the Baku trade counsellor, reports numerous complaints about problems, especially over height, for oversize transports by Türkiye-based carriers to Azerbaijan. It says the counsellor has contacted the Azerbaijan Land Transport Agency (AYNA) and the Highway Protection Service. It refers to Azerbaijani rules on the movement of oversize and heavy vehicles on public roads, special permits, fee tariffs and permitted dimensions and weights. The supplied text is truncated, so the specific limits and fees are not available.

**Where: Azerbaijan – public roads (specific roads not stated).**

**Operator action:** Before dispatch, confirm the current special-permit requirements, fees and height limits directly with AYNA or a local agent, and plan the route accordingly.

*Source: [denib.gov.tr](https://denib.gov.tr/en/duyuru-2026-330.html)*

### Belarus: narrow easing for EU-registered trucks from 1 December

Under a government decree, EU-registered trucks may from 1 December 2026 cross Belarus without cargo reloading or trailer swapping in certain cases: diplomatic cargo, goods for official use by representations of international organisations, and radioisotope products. Empty trucks travelling to load radioisotope products or reusable packaging for them are also allowed. The list of designated reloading and trailer-swap locations was updated. Restrictions on EU-registered trucks and tractor units have applied since 16 April 2022.

**Where: Belarus – transit across the national territory (on the monitored international freight corridors). · When: From 1 December 2026.**

**Operator action:** Check the decree text and the updated list of reloading locations before accepting any such transit job. For all other cargo, keep the existing reloading or trailer-swap requirements.

*Source: [Nasha Niva](https://nashaniva.com/en/409654) — Industry report — not an official authority notice*

### Denmark: authorities recommend making modular-combination scheme permanent; political decision pending

According to Lastbil Magasinet, the Danish Road Directorate (Vejdirektoratet) and the Road Safety and Transport Agency (Færdselsstyrelsen) have prepared a decision basis for a political decision on the current trial schemes for modular combinations (modulvogntog) and double-trailer combinations. The haulage association DTL welcomes the recommendation to make the modular-combination scheme permanent, but one proposal worries the industry. The article is paywalled, so that proposal is not identified in the supplied text.

**Where: Denmark – national trial schemes for modular and double-trailer combinations.**

**Operator action:** Keep operating under the current trial conditions and follow the political decision. Avoid fleet investments that rely on the outcome until it is confirmed.

*Source: [Lastbil Magasinet](https://www.lastbilmagasinet.dk/article/view/1258132/vognmaend_ser_store_gevinster_i_permanente_modulvogntog_men_et_forslag_bekymrer) — Industry report — regulatory/route conditions require confirmation with the competent authority*
